chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

When the legal punishment is carried out on a thief, he is exiled to another town. If a man steals and is not apprehended until he steals another time, then is seized, and the evidence comes and they testify against him concerning the first theft and the last theft, then his hand is cut off for the first theft, and his foot is not cut off for the last theft, because the witnesses testified against him together in a single proceeding regarding the first theft and the last theft before his hand had been cut off for the first theft. But if the witnesses testified against him for the first theft and his hand was cut off, then afterward they testified against him for the last theft, his left foot would be cut off.

key_terms.السَّارِقِ: the thief upon whom the legal ruling is applied
key_terms.السَّرِقَةِ الْأَخِيرَةِ: the later theft considered in relation to the first judgment
key_terms.السَّرِقَةِ الْأُولَى: the first theft for which the initial punishment is applied
key_terms.رِجْلُهُ الْيُسْرَى: his left foot, which is cut in the subsequent stage of punishment
key_terms.نُفِيَ: he was exiled or banished to another town

ai.seo_question: How is the hadd punishment applied if a thief committed multiple thefts before being caught?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling concerning the hadd punishment for theft and the order in which repeated theft cases are adjudicated. It distinguishes between multiple thefts proven together in one proceeding and thefts proven sequentially after the first punishment has already been carried out.
